newsitem.title: UK: UK's Clubhaus seeks fresh acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clubhaus seeks fresh acquisitions.

text.p: European golf course operator Clubhaus Plc said on Tuesday it was seeking fresh acquisitions and that it was looking at four targets in Britain.
"We are going to continue making acquisitions in the UK," chief operating officer Guy Buckley told reporters.
Speaking at a results briefing, Buckley said that Clubhaus would seek to make acquisitions before the peak summer season and that the targets would fit into its "Family Golf" portfolio.
Clubhaus operates some 10 golf clubs, seven of which are part of its "Premier" range and three of which are part of the less expensive brand aimed at families.
The company, which has operations in France and Germany, reported a pre-tax profit of 1.5 million stg in the period between November 1995 and December 1996.
Clubhaus joined the stock market in February 1996 after it was demerged from property group Ex-Lands.

Managing director Charlie Parker said that Clubhaus was seeking to build on its market position in Germany and had targeted two sites. However, he said that these were likely to be management deals rather than outright purchases.

The company is planning to introduce a membership card to link all of its clubs across Europe. It is also seeking a tie-in with a golf club in a warm weather location such as Spain or Portugal to offer golfers the chance to play while northern Europe freezes.
